waypoints.expectation: The FRONT-DOOR spawn (task 023, owner-sited): the chibi mayor on the decomposed-granite forecourt FACING THE WATER — open lawn running east to the Belmont Rocks steps and the blue lake with sailboats; the grey monument wall (gold letters, bronze ginkgo scatter) along the frame's right with white sitting blocks and the leaning boulder, the upsized WHERE NEXT suggestion box ahead-right, the crushed-limestone entrance path heading toward the lake, Divvy dock + Lakefront Trail behind-left. Must match baseline.png composition.

AIDS Garden Chicago: colorful flower beds around the two-lobe plaza loop (statue ring + southwest lawn lobe), with the 30-ft green Keith Haring figure sculpture dominating the scene. Lawn setting west of the rocks; the entrance monument fronts the trail at the garden's north edge.
The Belmont Rocks hangout: stepped revetment terraces stepping down to the lake, dotted with colorful towels, tilted umbrellas and coolers; open blue water east.

Diversey Point, the map's south corner: the 7-step terraced revetment curving from east-facing to south-facing, big south lawn behind, blue Chevron sculpture and/or corner pier nearby; skyline may read to the south.
Belmont Harbor basin: calm water with rows of moored sailboats (mooring cans), west-shore finger docks with boats, the treed spit peninsula east across the water.
The harbor pier deck: wooden planks over water at the basin edge, rails/lamp, boats and harbor water around it.
The yacht club on the west shore lawn: clubhouse building with a burgee pole facing the water, docks nearby.
The dog beach cove: a small rounded sand cove with fence and gates, dogs/fetch play on the sand, harbor water beyond; the trail passes north of the cove, never crossing the sand.
The Kwanusila totem pole on the inner lawn: a tall carved pole with painted figures and spread wings near the top, lawn and trees around it.

Bill Jarvis Bird Sanctuary: a dense dark woodland grove wrapped by an organic fence loop; inside are a winding limestone path, layered wildflowers and an elevated wooden viewing deck. Reads like a secret garden room.
The Waveland fieldhouse with its landmark clock tower — pitched-roof brick fieldhouse, square tower with clock faces — just inside the golf course's SE corner by the trail.
Sydney R. Marovitz golf course: fenced rolling fairways with greens, flags and bunkers stretching north; tee/green dressing, no buildings dominating.

From the elevated birdwatch DECK (the sanctuary's hero perch), looking west over the interior: the winding limestone loop and dappled clearings spread below through the trees, deck rail/planks framing the near foreground (the mayor standing on the platform, not fallen to the grass). Crucially the sanctuary reads BUSY WITH BIRDS — MULTIPLE birds visible at once across the layers (canopy / shrubs / ground / clearing edges): little chibi songbirds perched and flitting, and frequently a special sighting — a heron statue-still at a clearing edge, the woodpecker on the pale dead snag, a hovering hummingbird, or a cedar-waxwing flock. It must NOT read as an empty grove.

Standing in a Diversey hitting bay on the ground deck, the view DOWN the range (north): the open bay front framed by divider walls, the green fenced field receding under the tall perimeter net, distance boards; reads as a real enterable Topgolf-style bay you hit from — not scenery.

The 3-hole mini-golf course reads as a coherent place: three felt fairways (a dogleg, a loop hole, a windmill hole) with wood rails that HUG the felt edges (never crossing like pick-up sticks), each with a tee pad, a cup + flag, the windmill tower and the blue loop on their own holes, ringed by a low boundary fence with a MINI GOLF sign.
Wooden 'BELMONT HARBOR' sign readable, harbor water/docks context behind.
Wooden 'DOG BEACH' sign readable, standing on GRASS north of the sand cove (not in the sand), facing the trail.
Wooden 'BIRD SANCTUARY' sign readable by the sanctuary's west gate, dense grove behind.
Wooden 'WAVELAND FIELDHOUSE' sign readable on the trail side; clock tower visible behind.
Wooden 'YACHT CLUB' sign readable near the clubhouse lawn.
Wooden 'WAVELAND TENNIS COURTS' sign readable at the SE corner of the fenced 2x2 court block: green slabs, painted lines, sagging nets.
Wooden 'DIVERSEY RANGE & MINI GOLF' sign readable SW of the range; two-tier driving-range bays and/or the tall perimeter net behind.

The park-district suggestion box at KIOSK scale (owner upsize 2026-07-10): wood post, green painted body, gabled lid, brass mail slot, cream front label 'WHERE NEXT? — drop a suggestion / press E' legible — standing ahead-right of the new monument spawn on the forecourt's east lawn, monument wall and/or entrance path in frame. Reads at spawn distance, not birdhouse-tiny.

The AIDS Garden entrance monument per entrance-monument-sign.jpg (owner-sited near the garden Divvy dock): a low wide grey concrete/granite wall, gold 'AIDS Garden Chicago' letters FULLY legible on its north face — the leaning granite boulder sits mid-span WEST of the letters and never covers the 'A' (owner correction) — a quiet scatter of small bronze ginkgo-leaf plaques (names NOT legible — right at toon scale), two white limestone sitting blocks on a speckled grey-tan decomposed-granite forecourt, prairie grass flanking, a white globe lamp behind. The ONE and ONLY AIDS Garden sign in the game.

The plaza loop per aerial-path-structure.jpg: a TWO-LOBE peanut of crushed-limestone path — the ring around the green Haring statue's lawn plus a larger southwest lawn lobe — clearly NOT a plain circle; the connector joins from the west, MAIN skims the east point, and the entrance path heads off NE toward the lake. Flower beds and garden life around; statue upright on its pad.
The corner pier: a deck jutting SOUTH over open water from the corner-wrap revetment, lamp at its tip; skyline backdrop to the south, water under its flanks.
The harbor house: a small red-roofed harbor office building on the inner-park side of the basin.

John Henry's Chevron per chevron-closeup-IMG_0389: a TWO-TONE blue steel sculpture — pale powder-blue tapered upper mast (flaring to a beveled chisel tip) over a darker steel-blue base — plus a second leaning blade and slender square-section straight arms CROSSING like pick-up sticks (beams pass through, not a radial fan from one hub); green meadow lawn around the low pad, open lake water beyond the shore edge. Reads instantly against the sky.

The corner revetment per steps-cove-IMG_0394 / steps-to-pier-IMG_0395: broad weathered warm-gray limestone steps descending seaward toward the pier, GREEN GROWTH tufting the block joints, a rubble riprap toe at the waterline, and the cove inlet's water between the steps and the pier; lawn/Chevron above. The 7-step wrap geometry itself already reads true — judge the weathering, the toe rubble and the cove read.

Seawall furniture per 0395/0398/0399: from the corner pier deck, WHITE PIPE RAILING (posts + two thin horizontal rails, white) runs along the shore's top edge flanking the pier, white bollard posts line the pier deck edges, and a RED life ring on a post reads clearly on the deck; concrete apron underfoot (pale slab, not wood planks), tip lamp to the south.

The corner lawn per lawn-path-IMG_0398 + chevron-lawn-IMG_0396: a pale concrete path CURVES across the lawn toward the pier with park benches beside it FACING THE WATER, a worn brown dirt desire path parallels it on the seaward side, and scattered limestone sitting-stone blocks rest in the grass; the Chevron rises from the meadow; picnic/sunbather life reads as lived-in, not staged.

The harbor-mouth read per harbor-mouth-IMG_0399: from the pier's south end, the long TERRACED revetment recedes in a curve to the west, open water south with the skyline on the horizon, and the pier apron (bollards, red life ring, tip lamp) in the near frame. (The photo's finger docks belong to Diversey Harbor proper, off-map SW — not expected in frame.)
Arrival on the elevated Addison Red Line island platform (y 7.6): platform furniture/signage, twin tracks alongside, Wrigleyville streets below; down-the-platform framing, not clipped into walls.

THE shot: the red Wrigley Field marquee on the ROUNDED Clark & Addison corner, reading like the real sign per the owner ref: arched crown with 'WRIGLEY FIELD' set along the arc, small 'HOME OF' over large 'CHICAGO CUBS', art-deco scroll shoulders, white pinstripe trim, and a black rounded message board with DOT-MATRIX lettering (live message line). Behind it the facade reads as a looming GRANDSTAND, not a storefront (012/IMG_2333): green steel column rhythm rising to the rim, red-brick band + red-tile pent over the ground floor, arched-window band at the crown, and a flag ring (Chicago city flag among them) above the marquee. A Chicagoan should recognize THIS sign instantly.
The hand-turned green centerfield scoreboard high atop the bleachers (base ~18, top ~26.5): line-score grid, pennants above, no video boards (classic postcard Wrigley).

The Marquee Gate ON the rounded corner's apex under the marquee: gate recess in the curved cream facade, with the RED-BRICK corner apron paving the ground in front (the 009 signature Wrigley ground treatment), crowd/turnstile dressing.

The Gallagher Way gate set in the wedge's east bowl wall: gate recess with its green sign and red-brick pad on the plaza in front, ticket booth beside it; south of the gate the plaza visibly narrows toward the brick ticket-office mass.

The Addison Gate mid-block on the stadium's SOUTH face (owner placement correction; moved to x -252 with the 020 corner cut): maroon gate doors in a brick-framed recess with its green gate sign, and the green 'WELCOME TO THE FRIENDLY CONFINES' banner riding above it on the facade.

GATE D on the SE-corner diagonal (task 020): maroon gate doors with a green GATE D sign set in the ANGLED bowl wall, a green WRIGLEY FIELD board above, red-brick corner court in front, the grandstand crown wrapping the corner overhead — the gate faces the Sheffield & Addison intersection; the flat east (Sheffield) face beyond stays gateless red brick.

The Bleacher Gate on the CHAMFERED Sheffield & Waveland corner (009 rework): the gate faces the intersection at 45 degrees with its green BLEACHERS sign, fronted by a generous RED-BRICK plaza apron carrying the Harry Caray statue centered and OFF the sidewalk through-line, gate behind the statue per the owner reference; the green scoreboard rides above/behind the corner; Murphy's across the street.

The knothole (owner directive 2026-07-09): a screened opening in the red-brick LEFT-FIELD wall on WAVELAND at the ball-hawk corner (by the Kenmore axis), green frame + KNOTHOLE sign, where you can peek at the field inside.

The Addison stair doorway under the girder bridge now reads as the station head-house (refs/addison-station/): limestone portal frame proud of the abutment around the door, crowned by the real dark CTA sign band 'Addison 3600 N / 940 W' with the red Elevator tab and white Cubs-logo square; street passes beneath the bridge.

Murphy's Bleachers at the SE corner of Sheffield & Waveland reads as THE real bar (refs/murphys-bleachers/): a 2-storey blonde-brick mass with a cream fascia carrying big red MURPHY'S BLEACHERS letters and a rooftop deck, a 1-storey red-brick corner annex with the verdigris bronze sign band (baseball disc + MURPHY'S) and sage-green awning, a changeable-letter marquee board on a pole, and a fenced sidewalk beer garden with tables/umbrellas along Sheffield.

Engine 78 firehouse on Waveland reads as THE real 1915 house (refs/engine-78/): tan/olive-brown brick with limestone pilasters, string course, cornice and crown cartouche; ONE red-framed apparatus bay with the engine nosing out under a carved CITY OF CHICAGO FIRE DEPARTMENT lintel; red 2nd-floor awning; red side door; red planters, red hydrant and a bench on the apron; US + Chicago flags.

The Cubby Bear opposite the marquee corner reads as THE real bar (refs/cubby-bear/): blonde/tan-brick 2-storey corner block, black storefront fascia with window neon (no sign clipping past any face edge — issue 001), maroon corner door toward Clark & Addison, diamond THE CUBBY BEAR logo on both street faces, dark-green cornice, rooftop billboard on a steel truss above.

SLUGGERS on the west side of Clark: cream party-wall storefront with the yellow/red SLUGGERS sign band (+ WORLD CLASS SPORTS BAR script) and a FAST PITCH BATTING CAGES banner; the task-009 exterior stair and rooftop cage still read above the storefront; part of the glowing bar row.

SPORTS CORNER in the Clark bar row reads to type (refs/sports-corner/): cream/buff 3-storey front, vertical blue SPORTS CORNER blade sign readable from the street, navy awnings over a glassy ground floor, big glassy 2nd-floor windows, roof-deck railing on top.

CASEY MORAN'S in the Clark bar row: white/cream classical facade with arched 2nd-floor windows, dark-green sign band with gold CASEY MORAN'S lettering (shamrock neon kept), rooftop pergola/deck hint above.
THE DUGOUT in the Clark bar row: dark-brick 2-storey dive with a black storefront band, white hand-lettered THE DUGOUT sign, beer neon in the window, green awning.
A souvenir/cap stand on Addison by the station: caps, W flags, Cubs-blue merchandise on display.
A souvenir/cap stand on the Addison NORTH sidewalk mid-block, the stadium facade rising directly behind it.
A souvenir/cap stand on the Sheffield west sidewalk south of the Caray plaza, near the bleacher corner.
Statue Row on Gallagher Way's north edge fronting the Gallagher office block: four bronze statues on limestone pedestals (Ernie Banks first), the office mass closing the plaza behind them.

The Harry Caray statue CENTERED on the red-brick Caray plaza in front of the chamfered Bleacher Gate (009, per the owner reference): exuberant mic-aloft pose with glasses on a limestone pedestal, brick paving underfoot, the gate and its BLEACHERS sign behind, clear of the sidewalk through-lines.

Gallagher Way as the real WEDGE (task 019): Clark rushing past on the diagonal west edge; the west-stands bowl wall (brick base, green steel, crown) running near-N-S on the east; the plaza visibly WIDE at the north and NARROWING south to a full-height brick TICKET OFFICE mass that closes the south end (no open void). The floor reads designed: warm pavers with dark banding strips forming panels, a wedge-shaped lawn, tree planters along Clark, green bistro table sets (no orphaned scattered chairs), and a proper angled cornhole pair on legs on the lawn (raised hole-ends facing each other); splash pad clean on the pavers; statue row + video board at the north edge.

From THE climbable Waveland rooftop (y 9.6): rooftop bleacher rows looking over Waveland INTO the park — outfield, scoreboard and light towers visible over the LF wall; EAMUS CATULI building nearby. The scoreboard's near (back) face is DRESSED (012 legibility liberty): round clock + compact line-score panel read from up here; ivy legible on the outfield wall; no floating roof-ring slabs over the grandstand rim.

THE Sluggers rooftop batting cage (task 009): atop the lowered SLUGGERS bar, reachable by the exterior stair, a netted fast-pitch tunnel with the pitching machine and home plate sits on a rooftop deck the mayor can stand on. Reads as a real upstairs destination — not a street hut. The batter faces the park (east).

The street approach to Sluggers on Clark: the low 2-storey bar with a visible exterior stair climbing its street face to the rooftop batting cage above, and a 'BATTING CAGES UPSTAIRS ↑' sign at the base. The cage is a destination you walk up to, not furniture on the sidewalk.

A CPD street closure: blue wooden A-frame barricades ('POLICE LINE') with an officer NPC closing Addison east past the station; Lakeview backdrop buildings continue beyond — diegetic wall, not a void.

Addison midblock street canyon (double-wide game-day scale after 009): street enclosed on BOTH sides — station embankment/stalls one way, stadium facade and storefronts the other. Every commercial ground floor shows a DOOR and glazing; lamp posts and street furniture (meters/hydrant/newsboxes) set a rhythm; no blank single-color wall longer than ~8 m; crosswalks and signals read at the corners.

Sheffield midblock canyon (double-wide after 009): the stadium's RED-BRICK right-field wall on one side (012 — no gate/door visuals on this east face; the knothole moved to Waveland), rooftop-brownstone fronts (stoops, bay windows, doors) on the other. Furniture rhythm on the sidewalk; parked cars plausible; no bare prism walls.

Waveland midblock canyon (double-wide after 009): brownstone fronts with stoops/doors/cornices facing the stadium's RED-BRICK left-field wall (knothole at the ball-hawk corner after 012) and Engine 78; rooftop bleachers visible above; street furniture rhythm; no blank walls.

Clark St diagonal canyon (double-wide after 009): continuous bar-row storefronts (doors, glazing, awnings, neon at storefront height) on the west side, the Gallagher wedge opening behind the brick ticket-office mass on the east; pennant strings overhead attach to real anchors; furniture + signal presence; the street feels SURROUNDED, not like boxes beside a plane.

Clark & Addison, all four corners occupied and right: the marquee on its rounded corner (NE of the intersection — the stadium block is north of Addison, east of Clark), the Cubby Bear across Addison (SW), bar-row masses up Clark (NW), storefront fabric SE. No bare corner, no backdrop-grade box facing the intersection.

Sheffield & Addison, the FIELD corner done right: the stadium SE/right-field corner reads as its real angled/rounded mass with signage presence but NO gate/door visuals on the east face (owner placement correction, 012); a souvenir-store corner across Addison (Sports World-style); the station entrance relationship east; every corner holds something with intent.
Sheffield & Waveland: the chamfered Bleacher Gate + Caray plaza on the stadium corner, Murphy s Bleachers across, rooftop brownstones up Sheffield — the classic bleacher-corner tableau, no voids.
Clark & Waveland: stadium NW corner treatment on one side, brownstone/bar fabric across Clark and along Waveland toward Engine 78 — corners read as a real neighborhood junction, not backdrop.

A period-plausible painted ROOFTOP AD BOARD atop the west Waveland brownstone (the one WITHOUT the EAMUS CATULI banner), above its rooftop bleachers on a steel-leg frame, angled down toward the street: weathered-cream board reading 'SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT ♥' in oxblood serif on the left with a crisp black-on-white QR panel on the right. Reads as a real Wrigley rooftop billboard, not a UI popup; the QR must be sharp and undistorted enough to scan (mechanically decoded to the Ko-fi URL by tools/decode-qr.mjs).

Inside the Red Line car, the 'SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT ♥' ad placard on the north end wall (the transit-car ad precedent, like the Wrigley's Spearmint card): a cream poster with red frame, the header over a large crisp black-on-white QR and the ko-fi.com/jimbobuildsope caption, read head-on down the car's length and clear of the grab poles. The QR must be sharp enough to scan (mechanically decoded to the Ko-fi URL by tools/decode-qr.mjs).
